english.note: This is the all-purpose choice for physically obstructing a person, object, or route.
Use this for the all-purpose idea of physically obstructing a route or opening so nothing can pass.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for getting in the way of someone or something.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for physically blocking someone or holding up an action or process.
This is the colloquial all-purpose choice when something blocks, impedes, or prevents an action or process.
Use this as the all-purpose spoken verb when someone or something holds up, stops, or hinders progress.
Use this for stopping or holding back a person or thing from doing something.
Use this when the emphasis is on holding back development or progress.
Use this when an obstacle actively blocks or restricts progress, rather than simply burdening someone.
Use this when disrupting means hindering or obstructing, especially when progress is blocked rather than someone being verbally interrupted.
Use this when someone or something prevents, obstructs, or interrupts another person from doing something.
Use this when something holds someone or something back, delays progress, or obstructs movement.

examples.english: That truck is there to bar the road.
examples.jyutping: bou6 fo3 ce1 zo2 zyu6 tiu4 lou6

examples.english: The car is parked at the entrance to block people from getting in and out.
examples.traditional: 架車泊喺門口，阻住人哋出入。
examples.jyutping: gaa3 ce1 bok6 hai2 mun4 hau2 zo2 zyu6 jan4 dei6 ceot1 jap6
